- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 7-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above recent high.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.4) and price is falling, model underreacts; add 1–3% upward bias to prevent premature mean reversion.
- Model frequently overcorrects after strong downward moves; if true outcome shows recovery within 3–5 days, forecast should be slightly below prior low.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.5), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values.
- When sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.4 to 0.05), model often fails to anticipate sharp sell-off; reduce forecast by 5–10% and add 1–2 day lagged correction.
